newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines arrests top anti-APEC leftist leader.
newsitem.headline: Philippines arrests top anti-APEC leftist leader.

text.p: Philippine soldiers on Tuesday arrested one of the country's top leftist leaders in what his supporters said was a move to neutralise opponents of this month's APEC summit.

Filemon Lagman, who heads a workers' group that military intelligence reports have accused of plotting to disrupt the November 25 summit, was arrested in a hotel in the Manila suburb of Quezon City, an army spokesman said.

The spokesman said Lagman was detained in connection with the killing of a policeman in 1992 and denied his arrest was linked to the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which will be attended by U.S. President Bill Clinton and leaders of 17 other member economies.
"Contrary to speculation by some sectors, Lagman's arrest is not connected with APEC security preparations," army spokesman Colonel Leopoldo Maligalig said.

Manila newspapers have said the supposed anti-APEC plans by leftist groups include fomenting strikes among workers in the hotel, transport and telecommunications sectors, which all provide key support services to the summit and to the ministerial meeting that precedes it.

Lagman is chairman of the leftist BMP (Coalition of Filipino Workers) which is organising an anti-APEC workers' meeting coinciding with the summit, which is being held at Subic Bay north of the capital.

The workers' meeting, one of four conferences being organised by private groups in parallel with the summit, is to be climaxed by a motorcade and march from Manila to Subic Bay to be attended by thousands of workers, BMP officials said.
"The military wants to neutralise him for the APEC ... and deliver a strong signal to all other anti-APEC groups," BMP spokesman Wilson Fortaleza told Reuters.
"Maybe this is only the beginning of a bigger plan," Fortaleza said, expressing concern that Lagman's arrest might be followed by crackdowns on other leftist leaders.
The military has also accused Lagman of heading a death squad blamed by the government for the killing of several hundred policemen, soldiers and local officials in recent years.
Lagman was meeting some people at the Sulo Hotel when military agents arrested him, Fortaleza said.
The leftist leader was arrested in 1994 on charges of involvement in the killing of several policemen by the death squad but was freed on bail and the case was never pursued.
Even while free, Lagman complained to reporters that he was constantly followed and harassed.
His brother, opposition congressman Edcel Lagman, tried to visit the leftist leader at the army camp where he was being detained but was not allowed in.
"This is definitely connected with APEC," the lawmaker told reporters.
President Fidel Ramos, a former career soldier and armed forces chief, had earlier pledged to exercise "maximum tolerance" towards anti-APEC activities.
Critics, however, have accused APEC organisers of tactics reminiscent of the authoritarian rule of late president Ferdinand Marcos in their determination to prevent any disruptions to the meeting.
